title: もらう and てもらう: the receiving verb
summary: もらう is a pull-verb: you receive something or an action, and the giver takes に. It behaves like the receptive, not like くれる.

blocks.text: もらう is usually grouped with あげる and くれる, but the grouping hides how it really works. **あげる** gives up; **くれる** gives down to me or my group. Both are tied to a particular giver and receiver. (A warning: 〜てあげる sounds like you are doing a favor, so it is not polite toward a superior.) **もらう** is also "downloading", but it is a **pull** where you take the initiative, and it works much more like the receptive れる / られる (lesson 13).
With a noun, もらう need not name any giver at all. If you do name the giver, mark them with **に** (or から).

blocks.en: (I) got ten thousand yen. (no giver needed)

blocks.text: に: where it goes, or where it comes from
The same に points in opposite directions. With a push verb it is the place the thing travels to. With a pull verb like もらう it is the place the thing comes from.

blocks.jp: メアリーにボールを投げた。
blocks.en: (I) threw the ball to Mary. (に = where it goes)
(I) got flowers from a friend. (に = where it comes from)

blocks.text: After the て-form, もらう means "get someone to do it for me". The carriage is the receiver, and the person who does the action takes に, exactly like the doer in a receptive sentence. The difference is in the feeling: **られる** says something simply happened to you, **てもらう** says you brought it about.
先生に見てもらった。 (I) got the teacher to look at it.

rows: The teacher praised me. (it happened to me)
I got the teacher to look at it. (I asked)

blocks.text: Many English renderings are misleading. With no doer named, none is implied.

blocks.jp: お医者さんに見てもらう。
blocks.en: (I) have a doctor look at me. (not just "see a doctor")

blocks.text: The receiver need not be you
くれる only suits you or your group. もらう has no such restriction. You can say about another person that they received something or got something done.

blocks.jp: 弟は兄に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
blocks.en: My younger brother got his older brother to help with his homework.

blocks.jp: 髪を切ってもらったほうがいいよ。
blocks.en: You should get your hair cut.

items: **もらう** = receive (a pull); the giver or doer takes **に**.
**Nをもらう** need not mention a giver; **Vてもらう** = get someone to do it.
It is closest to the receptive but adds "I brought it about".
Unlike くれる, the receiver may be a third person.

questions.instruction: Who gave the clothes?
questions.note: The giver is marked with に; the receiver is the carriage.
questions.en: I got clothes from my older sister.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says the speaker got it done by asking someone?
options: 兄に宿題を教えてもらった。
questions.note: 〜てもらう means "I brought it about"; the others just happened.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 私は兄＿＿自転車を貸してもらった。
questions.note: The one who does the action takes に, as in a receptive sentence.
questions.en: I got my older brother to lend me his bicycle.

questions.instruction: In a もらう sentence, who is the carriage?
questions.note: もらう is a pull: the receiver takes the initiative.

questions.instruction: What separates 〜てもらう from the receptive 〜られる?
options: The ending of the verb only
てもらう says you brought it about; られる says it happened to you
てもらう is always rude
questions.note: The difference is in the feeling: initiative versus things simply happening.

questions.instruction: Which verb can describe something a third person received?
questions.note: くれる only suits you or your group; もらう has no such limit.

questions.instruction: Who cut the hair?
questions.prompt: 妹は母に髪を切ってもらった。
questions.note: The doer is marked with に.
questions.en: My little sister had Mother cut her hair.

questions.instruction: Does the sentence name who did it?
questions.prompt: 私は駅まで送ってもらった。
options: No, the doer is not named
questions.note: The doer is simply not named; context tells us who gave the ride.
questions.en: I got a ride to the station.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: The giver takes に (or から).
questions.en: I got a book from a friend.

questions.instruction: Does this sentence have to name the giver?
questions.note: With a thing, もらう names no giver.

questions.instruction: What does it mean that もらう is a "pull"?
options: The giver gives down to me
questions.note: あげる gives up and くれる gives down; もらう pulls.

questions.instruction: Which verb gives "down to me or my group"?
questions.note: くれる is tied to a giver and a receiver in my group.

questions.instruction: Who made breakfast?
questions.prompt: 母に朝ご飯を作ってもらった。
questions.note: The person marked with に did the action.

questions.instruction: How do you say "get someone to help me"?
questions.note: て-form + もらう.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is wrong?
options: 先生にかばんをもらった。
先生をかばんをもらった。
先生からかばんをもらった。
先生に本を貸してもらった。
questions.note: The giver takes に or から, never を.

questions.instruction: Who is the carriage of もらった?
questions.prompt: 姉は友達に写真を見てもらった。
questions.note: The receiver (姉) is the carriage; 友達 takes に.
questions.en: My older sister had a friend look at the photo.

questions.instruction: Which sentence marks the doer correctly?
options: 兄に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
兄を宿題を手伝ってもらった。
兄が宿題を手伝ってもらった。
兄で宿題を手伝ってもらった。
questions.note: The doer of the action takes に.

questions.instruction: Tap the person who did the action
questions.note: に marks the doer in 〜てもらう.
questions.en: I had my mother teach me cooking.

questions.instruction: Tap the helper verb that says "I brought it about"
questions.note: もらう after the て-form means getting someone to do it.
questions.en: I got a friend to take me to the station.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I had my brother lend me a bicycle.
questions.note: The doer takes に, the thing takes を.
questions.en: I had my brother lend me a bicycle.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I had the teacher look at my photo.
questions.note: てもらう: に marks the one who looks.
questions.en: I had the teacher look at the photo.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: My brother got a book from a friend.
questions.note: The giver takes に; もらった is the engine.
questions.en: My brother got a book from a friend.
